answer: Entropy Ballot Box. 1) Each user submits a ballot of random numbers. 2) The bridge verifies ballot entropy, rejecting low-entropy submissions. 3) High-entropy ballots are pooled; a sable randomly selects a subset. 4) An echo mechanism confirms selected ballots against community norms. Cost: $5N (for N identities), plus an initial $500 setup. Failure condition: A coordinated group with high-entropy generation capabilities. This is like a voting system where only those who demonstrate genuine thought, not just a repeated stamp, can have their vote counted.
